title: Symmetrization resistance for exponential and geometric distributions
summary: Given a random variable $X$, an independent random variable $Y$ is called a symmetrizer of $X$ if their sum $X+Y$ is symmetric about the origin. The study of symmetrization resistance asks whether every such $Y$ must contain at least as much randomness as $X$. This problem was previously investigated for binary random variables in terms of variance and Shannon entropy. In this paper, we establish sharp symmetrization resistance results for exponential and geometric distributions.
